Program : 

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    void *a = malloc(0x20);   // 1st malloc: heap gets initialized
    void *b = malloc(0x20);
    void *c = malloc(0x100);

    free(a);   // -> tcache (size 0x30) 
    free(b);   
    free(c);   // -> tcache (0x110)
    void *d = malloc(0x20);   // reuses b 
    printf("%p %p %p %p %p\n", a, b, c,d);
    return 0;
}
```

lower bite : 1 = PREV_INUSE

----------------------------------------------------
free()
- libC generate a random key (tcache_key) (in my version, this is a random but generated once time)  
- if random key == key --> double free detected. Stop. 
- if not, just free a chunk --> So if we can use a vuln use-after-free to write key, just 1 byte, it will allow us to free 2 times a chunk

WHY tcache_perthread_struct is 0x300 ? 

typedef struct tcache_perthread_struct {
    char counts[TCACHE_MAX_BINS];       // or uint16_t counts[TCACHE_MAX_BINS]
    tcache_entry *entries[TCACHE_MAX_BINS];
} tcache_perthread_struct;


Because in x86_64, a total tcache_perthread_struct = 0x280. Need to + 0x10 for header = 0x290
Because chunk sizes must be aligned to 0x20 bytes ---> next size = 0x300

the structure of tcache: 
- header : size : (0x10)
- counts array location: 0x5555555591b0 - 0x555555559240
- entries array location: 0x555555559250 
- First chunk address: 0x555555559010

Chunk a:
FW PTR = 0x0000000555555559 because the program is protected by safe linking
If it isn't protected by safe linking, it will be a normal addr 
FW PTR = (Addresse of pointer >> 12) xor NEXT_ADDR
FW PTR = (0x0000555555559010 >> 12) xor 0 # (NOT have next_addr yet) 
==> FW PTR = 0x0000555555559


Key = 0xdfb52cfdeee2f594 : random value to protect double free (Dont know what is that)

FW_PTR = (Addresse of pointer >> 12) ^ NEXT_ADDR

Because we malloc(0x20), so the program look for tcache[0], get the addr 0x0000555555559040, free the key, and change the value of tcache[0]. 
Because : FW_PTR = (ADDR >> 12) ^ Next_addr
So we know FW_PTR, ADDR ==> we will know Next_addr 
Next_addr = FW_PRT ^ (ADDR >> 12)
Next_addr = 0x000055500000c549 ^ (0x0000555555559040 >> 12)
>>> hex(0x000055500000c549 ^ (0x00005555555590\
40 >> 12))
'0x555555559010'
